title: `entire doctor` stuck-session prompt bypasses `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()`, so it blocks in scripts and CI

verdict.rationale: The stuck-session prompt was written as a huh select with Condense/Discard/Skip, and nothing in the evidence shows anyone chose for it to block when non-interactive. The non-interactive guard was deliberately added only to checkGitHooks ('doctor is a diagnostic an agent or CI job runs unattended, so it must neither block on a confirm'), which suggests the older prompt was simply missed rather than exempted.

feat(doctor): check and repair stale git hooks

`.git/hooks` is the one hook surface a user cannot see going wrong. Agent hook
configs are committed files that turn up in a diff; git hooks are per-clone and
untracked, so pulling a release that changes hook generation never touches them.
A hook left by the removed local-dev mode still carries Entire's marker, so it
looks installed while naming a launcher inside the working tree that is gone —
and because that shape got no availability guard while pre-push propagates exit
codes, the symptom is `git push` being rejected. Doctor had no git-hook check at
all, so the place a user looks after a rejected push said nothing.

Unlike the sibling agent hook checks this one repairs rather than only warning:
the reinstall is content-idempotent, backs up any foreign hook it displaces, and
writes exactly what the next turn-start would write anyway. It degrades to
warn-only when there is nobody to ask, naming `--force` instead — doctor is a
diagnostic an agent or CI job runs unattended, so it must neither block on a
confirm nor rewrite a repo's hooks unasked. An existing bare-`doctor` test caught
that: without the guard the prompt fails to open a TTY and doctor exits 1.

Distinguishing "no hooks" from "ours but stale" needs more than a bool, so this
adds strategy.GitHookState (Absent/Current/Outdated), mirroring
agent.HookConfigState so both hook surfaces share one vocabulary.
IsGitHookInstalled keeps meaning "current" for EnsureSetup.

fix(doctor): only treat missing git hooks as a problem where Entire is set up

doctor runs in any git repository, and `--force` means "don't ask me", not "take
over this repo". Reported by trail finding 01a000fc-37af: checkGitHooks treated
GitHooksAbsent as actionable with no check that Entire had ever been enabled
here, so `entire doctor --force` in a repo that merely had `entire` on PATH
backed up that repo's own pre-push hook and installed all five of Entire's.
Reproduced before fixing.

Missing hooks are now only reported where settings exist in either scope. The
sibling checks already held this line — checkHookDrift stays silent on
HooksAbsent, checkCodexHookTrust returns early with no codex hooks file — so this
check was the outlier.

IsSetUpAny rather than IsSetUpAndEnabled: a repo that ran `entire disable` still
wants working hooks, because the hooks themselves are what no-op while disabled.
GitHooksOutdated stays actionable regardless of settings — a hook carrying
Entire's marker means this repo opted in at some point, and a stale one is
actively broken rather than merely absent.

fix: propagate errors instead of swallowing in push, doctor, and post-commit paths

Three error-handling fixes from PR review:

1. Push path (push_common.go): reconciliation failure now returns an error
   instead of warning-and-continue. Proceeding to tree merge on disconnected
   branches would silently combine unrelated histories.

2. Doctor command (doctor.go): metadata check failure now propagates to
   the return value (non-zero exit). Previously, `entire doctor` could
   report success when the recommended repair path itself failed.

3. Post-commit hook (manual_commit_hooks.go): filesChangedInCommit now
   falls back to go-git tree walk when git diff-tree fails, instead of
   returning an empty map that breaks downstream condensation logic.

The cli and strategy packages each carried a private copy of
canPromptInteractively() with identical TTY-detection and
ENTIRE_TEST_TTY override semantics. strategy cannot import cli (import
cycle), so duplication was previously the cheap workaround — but it
means the two copies silently drift apart on every refactor.

interactive, which depends only on os. Both cli (attach, explain
summary provider, login, setup) and strategy (manual_commit_rewind)
now import and call interactive.CanPromptInteractively().

Test coverage moved from setup_test.go (which tested the cli copy) to
interactive/interactive_test.go, preserving the three env-var scenarios
(forced on, forced off, non-"1" value).

Isolated package with no cli/strategy dependencies means future shared
TTY/interactivity helpers (such as the duplicated isAccessibleMode)
have an obvious home when the scope is right.

Report legacy shadow branches in doctor instead of deleting them

Session start deleted strict-shape legacy shadow branches
(entire/<7+hex>-<6hex>) once per repository, recording a marker in the
git common dir. Deleting refs behind the user's back on an ordinary
session start is not something an upgrade should do, so that pass goes:
removeLegacyShadowBranches, CleanupLegacyShadowBranches, its marker,
deleteLegacyShadowBranchesIfUnchanged and checkedOutBranches are removed
with their tests. gitrepo.ParseWorktreeBranches stays; the resume picker
uses it.

`entire doctor` gains a check that reports the strict-shape branches,
names `entire clean` as the remedy, and deletes them itself under
--force or a confirmed prompt (doctor's existing fix flag; there is no
--fix). Deletion goes through DeleteBranchCLI (`git branch -D`), which
refuses a branch checked out in any worktree; doctor reports such a
branch and keeps it. `entire clean` is unchanged. README.md and
docs/security-and-privacy.md said the branches are deleted automatically
at the first session start, and implied plain `entire clean` removes the
bare entire/<commit> form; plain clean removes only the strict form and
--all also removes the bare one.
